newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa's Mbeki heads to Angola for talks.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Mbeki heads to Angola for talks.

text.p: A South African delegation headed by Deputy President Thabo Mbeki flew to Luanda on Monday for talks on Angola's peace process, a foreign affairs official said.
The two-day visit will include talks with the government and representatives of the UNITA former rebel movement.

It follows a meeting of South African cabinet ministers and Angolan Foreign Minister Venancio de Moura in Pretoria on Friday. Earlier this month UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi met a delegation led by President Nelson Mandela.
De Moura was on a tour of southern African countries to invite regional heads of state to attend the inauguration of Angola's unity government, scheduled for January 25.
"De Moura also came to personally invite President Mandela to attend Saturday's inauguration," the official told Reuters.
The South African delegation would urge both parties to push forward with the January 25 inauguration despite outstanding disagreement on some matters, he said.
Peace mediators are hoping for agreement this week on Savimbi's role in the unity government -- probably as "principal adviser with executive powers", diplomatic sources said.
UNITA has already rejected a position for Savimbi as deputy president in the government.
The meeting with Savimbi earlier this month drew sharp response from the Angolan government, which accused Mandela of interfering in U.N.-supervised mediation to end Angola's 20-year civil war.
Diplomats in Luanda said South Africa's willingness to help push forward Angola's slow-moving peace process should in the long term prove helpful.
